messages:
sam: noticed p99 token latency spikes on aap-sg1 dedicated slice since 03:05 UTC. GPU util unchanged but network metrics show long tx queues and high softirq time.
rachel: same, our models serving small, chatty requests are the ones affected. looks like packet-amplification from many tiny egress writes.
diego: host metrics: tx_queue_len=11200, softirq_pct=0.28, tx_drops=320. NIC IRQ handling is pegged.
noah: ops-bot: recommend throttling tenant with heaviest egress. candidate tenant t-88 has the top egress footprint.
sam: can we attach a temporary egress cap and observe? migration will cause backfill churn.
rachel: apply 8Mbps policer to t-88, and mark the host as egress-guard for scheduler to avoid new heavy-egress placements.
diego: applied policer id pol-900. within 90s p99 fell from 520ms -> 170ms. good.
sam: action items:
- short: policer automation + host flag (egress-guard)
- mid: scheduler weight influenced by host.egress_health (softirq, tx_queue)
- long: consider tenant-routing preference (prefer regions with spare NIC headroom for heavy egress)
rachel: note on cost: migrating a noisy tenant off a 8-GPU slice increases backfill churn ~0.4 GPU-hours/day. still cheaper than repeated SLO violations for that slice.
diego: I'll draft a small PR to emit host.egress_softirq_ratio and host.tx_queue_len and a tiny scheduler heuristic to lower weights when those exceed thresholds.
infra-bot: created INC-2091 (aap-sg1-egress-tail). responders: sam,rachel,diego.
